1225735704942125060.a: @SwiftOnSecurity CP/M is a good example of business computers taking advantage of the lack of info. They were binary compatible but each computer brand/model used a different disk format. Commodore C128 read all CP/M disks years too late to market where Microsoft DOS standardized the disk format.

1225737194863722496.a: @SwiftOnSecurity Users in the know realized they could load a disk driver on any CP/M machine to run programs from a competitors computer. Where would a consumer get this driver? A BBS someone told them about? They needed a modem and dumptruck of cash to pay long distance phone fees to download.

1225742821778448385.a: @SwiftOnSecurity I think it can be summarized as a get rich quick scheme based on disinfo, information blackout.
